label: Saturday, November 7, 2026 · Week-in-review edition
intro: Friday's partial rebound capped the worst week since early June: tech fell 7% and energy 11% over five sessions, and the Nasdaq stayed in a correction. The October jobs beat at 165,000 softened the landing, but it also pushed yields and December rate-hike odds right back up.

items.title: Nasdaq and S&P 500 rebound, Dow slips to cap bruising week for AI stocks
items.take: Friday closed with the S&P up 0.7% and the Nasdaq up 1.6%, but both wrapped their worst week since June 5, with tech down 7% and energy 11% over five sessions. Yardeni Research calls Thursday's selloff overdone and is sticking with a 7,900 year-end target on the S&P.

items.title: Stocks mixed, yields up on surging U.S. job growth
items.take: The 165,000 jobs print came in far above consensus, and yields climbed with it as rate-hike odds rose. The VIX topped 28 on Thursday, its highest since March, though Schwab's technicians note traditional benchmarks now show oversold conditions.

items.title: US tech stocks post modest recovery after worst day in 19 months
items.take: The Nasdaq clawed back 1.5% after Thursday's 5.5% plunge, with Rocket Lab up 12.5%, Airbnb up 11.7%, AMD up 9.3% and Intel up 8.9%. London wasn't so lucky: the FTSE 100 closed down 1% at 10,673 as AI concerns lingered.

items.title: Airbnb jumps on raised forecast, Atlassian sinks, Bitcoin steadies
items.take: Airbnb jumped 12% on a raised full-year revenue forecast while Atlassian sank 14% on its first-quarter results. Bitcoin settled near $75,600 after a 6% plunge from above $80,000, and Goldman cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 on the hawkish Fed outlook.

items.title: AI-tied sell-off slows as markets end week mixed
items.take: The week ended mixed as the AI-tied selloff slowed, with value and yield factors outperforming while growth sold off hard. Bargain hunting surfaced in the beaten-down areas, though commentators kept cautioning that no-earnings speculative names remain vulnerable.

items.title: Podcast: AI blues, Musk under the microscope, housing hope
items.take: This weekend's rotation pick is the markets edition of What's News, out Saturday morning: the AI rout's fallout, scrutiny on Musk after the midterms, and the one bright spot in housing.
